# bugs #3986: Warning 158 for constant sums, differences, and left shifts whose value fits in the char that is assigned

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3986/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply after the patch for local 0013. Confirm the new warnings under Decision. Bugs #2733, #2877, and #3094 have this cause.
- Patch: [bugs-3986.patch](../../patches/bugs-3986.patch), commit [`f955bae8b`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/f955bae8b9ad37f7d01b4a986ef980754f154ce4). Apply after `local-0013.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The declaration of the ticket, `uint8_t Foo = 30*8 - 1;` in a function, gets warning 158,
"overflow in implicit constant conversion", and its value 239 fits. The ticket calls the message
an error. On r17193 for mcs51, constant sums, differences, and left shifts that are assigned to a
char object or passed for a char parameter get the warning for some values that fit, and compile
without it for some values that do not fit. For an unsigned char `u` and a signed char `s`,
`u = 30 * 8 - 1`, `u = 127 + 1`, `u = 1 << 7`, and the call `g (30 * 8 - 1)` get the warning.
`u = 200 + 100`, `u = 255 + 1`, `s = 100 + 100`, and `s = 1 << 7` compile without it, and
`u = 1 << 8` gets warning 116 without a line number. The byte that the code stores is correct.

## Cause

When a value is assigned to a char, `decorateType` in `src/SDCCast.c` gives the operands of `+`,
`-`, and `<<` the result type char, so that the operation is done in 8 bits. For two literal
operands it casts them with `addCast` before `valPlus`, `valMinus`, or `valShift` computes the
constant. `addCast` makes an int literal a signed char, and the constant is computed in char.
`30 * 8 - 1` becomes -17, `1 << 7` becomes -128, and `200 + 100` becomes 44. `checkTypes` in
`src/SDCCicode.c` checks the range of that constant against the type of the left operand. In bug
#2733 a maintainer names the propagation of `RESULT_TYPE_CHAR` as the cause.

## Fix

In these three places `decorateType` applies the integer promotions when both operands are
literals and the result type is char. The constant is computed in int, and `cheapestVal` reduces
its type as it does for a product. `cheapestVal` gives the values 0 and 1 the type `bool`, and two
functions in `src/SDCCval.c` computed a wrong constant from a `bool` literal. `valBitwise` now
makes the result of an unsigned char literal and a `bool` literal an unsigned char, and
`valUnaryPM` promotes a `bool` literal to int. Without these two changes,
`u = ((unsigned char) 1 << 7) | ((unsigned char) 1 << 0)` and `s = -(2 - 1)` would get warning 158
with the patch. The two changes also correct `int i = (unsigned char) 0x80 | (2 - 1)`, which gave
-127.

## Decision

- With the patch, statements that r17193 compiles without warning 158 get it, because their
  value does not fit. Examples are `u = 200 + 100`, `u = 255 + 1`, `s = 127 + 1`,
  `s = 1 << 7`, and `u = 1 << 8`. On r17193, 12000 random constant expressions that are assigned
  to an unsigned char or a signed char were compiled with and without the patch. The patch
  removes the warning from 534 statements whose value fits and adds it to 2205 statements whose
  value does not fit. The byte that the code stores is equal with and without the patch for every
  statement.
- The complement of a constant is computed in 8 bits when the result type is char, with and
  without the patch, and `u = ~0x80` stores 0x7f without a warning. The patch computes a sum from
  that 8-bit value in int. `signed char s = ~0x80 + 1`, whose C value is -128, gets warning 158
  with the patch, and `unsigned char u = 7 + ~128`, whose C value is -122, does not. Without the
  patch it is the reverse. 9 of the 12000 statements change in this direction. 4 of them get the
  warning for a value that fits, and 5 lose it for a value that does not fit. 8 have such a sum,
  and the ninth has `(signed char) 127 ^ (unsigned char) 200`. The patch does not change the case
  of `~` in `decorateType`.
- Constants from 128 to 255 are unsigned char literals with the patch, where they were negative
  signed char literals. An expression that uses the value of an assignment gets the literal
  without a conversion, which is the fault of local 0013. For a volatile signed char `s`,
  `i = s = 100 + 100` sets `i` to 200 with this patch alone, where r17193 sets it to -56. With the
  patch for local 0013 applied first, `i` is -56.

## Verification

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-3986.c` has 5 cases. Compiled by r17193 for mcs51, it has 30 failures,
which are 21 warnings for values that fit and 9 statements without a warning whose value does not
fit. With the patches of this report up to this one applied to r17200, the diagnostics suite has 0
failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The regression suite has 0
failures for host, stm8, ucz80, and six mcs51 variants: the small, medium, large, and huge models,
and `--stack-auto` with the small and large models. The other ports were not built.

The patch changes code where 8-bit arithmetic has such a constant as an operand. The run above was
compared with r17200 and the earlier patches of this report, without the patch for local 0013 and
this patch. The assembly of three regression tests differs in each mcs51 variant, and one of them
is the effect of local 0013. `bug3475656.c` has `iTmp - 10 + 'A'`. Its code is 2 bytes larger for
mcs51-small and from 1 to 17 bytes smaller for the five other variants, stm8, and ucz80. In
`regtrack.c` only the spacing of one instruction differs. The library function `__ltoa` has
`c += 'A' - '9' - 1` and is one `mov` instruction shorter in each of the six mcs51 models, and the
test `ltoa` is 20 bytes smaller in the five variants other than mcs51-small. The other library
assembly files are identical for mcs51, stm8, and z80.

## Related

- Bugs #2733, #2877, and #3094 report this cause. Without the patch, `unsigned char c = 1 << 7;`
  in a function, `0x80 | 0x00 | (0x01 << 2)`, `24 + EXCESS`, and the argument `192 + 41` of these
  tickets get warning 158. With the patch on r17200 they compile for mcs51 without a warning.
- `valBitwise` computes char literals of different signedness in signed char, with and without the
  patch. `int i = -1 & (30 * 8)` gives -16, and `u = (unsigned char) 0x80 | ~(1 << 7)` gets warning
  158. The patch does not change this.
